title: एकोनषष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 59 · Fourth day: Bhima and the Kaurava brothers

summary.en: Duryodhana urges all his troops against Bhima, who stands unmoved like Mount Meru and wades through the fallen. Bhurishravas, seeing the Kaurava chariots driven off, charges in.
summary.kn: ಭೀಮನನ್ನು ಕೊಲ್ಲಿರೆಂದು ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ ಎಲ್ಲ ಸೈನ್ಯವನ್ನು ಪ್ರೇರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಭೀಮ ಮೇರುವಿನಂತೆ ಅಚಲನಾಗಿ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಕೌರವ ರಥಗಳು ಓಡುವುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡ ಭೂರಿಶ್ರವ ನುಗ್ಗುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: दुर्योधन सारी सेना को भीम पर चढ़ाता है, और भीम मेरु की तरह अचल खड़े रहते हैं। कौरव रथों को भागते देख भूरिश्रवा आक्रमण करता है।
summary.te: భీమునిపై పడమని దుర్యోధనుడు అన్ని సేనలను పురికొల్పుతాడు; భీముడు మేరువులా నిశ్చలంగా నిలుస్తాడు. కౌరవ రథాలు పారిపోవడం చూసి భూరిశ్రవుడు దూసుకువస్తాడు.
summary.ta: பீமனைக் கொல்லுங்கள் என்று துரியோதனன் எல்லாப் படைகளையும் தூண்ட, பீமன் மேரு போல் அசையாது நிற்கிறான். கௌரவத் தேர்கள் விரட்டப்படுவதைக் கண்ட பூரிசிரவஸ் பாய்கிறான்.
summary.ml: ഭീമനെതിരെ എല്ലാ സൈനികരെയും ദുര്യോധനൻ അയയ്ക്കുന്നു; മേരു പർവതംപോലെ അനങ്ങാതെ നിൽക്കുന്ന ഭീമൻ വീണുകിടക്കുന്നവരെ ചവിട്ടി മുന്നേറുന്നു. കൗരവ രഥങ്ങൾ പിന്തിരിയുന്നത് കണ്ട് ഭൂരിശ്രവസ്സ് പാഞ്ഞടുക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.59; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
तस्मिन्हते गजानीके पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव ।
भीमसेनं घ्नतेत्येवं सर्वसैन्यान्यचोदयत् ॥

meaning.en: When that elephant army was destroyed, your son Duryodhana urged all his divisions: "Kill Bhimasena!"

verses.text:
ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि तव पुत्रस्य शासनात् ।
अभ्यद्रवन्भीमसेनं नदन्तं भैरवान्रवान् ॥

meaning.en: Then, by your son's command, all the divisions rushed at Bhimasena as he roared terrible roars.

verses.text:
तं बलौघमपर्यन्तं देवैरपि दुरुत्सहम् ।
आपतन्तं सुदुष्पारं समुद्रमिव पर्वणि ॥

meaning.en: That endless flood of troops, hard to bear even for gods, bore down like a sea at the full moon, impossible to cross.

verses.text:
रथनागाश्वकलिलं शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादितम् ।
अथानन्तमपारं च नरेन्द्रस्तिमितह्रदम् ॥

meaning.en: It was a tangle of chariots, elephants and horses, resounding with conches and dundubhis, boundless and shoreless, with kings for its still depths.

verses.text:
तं भीमसेनः समरे महोदधिमिवापरम् ।
सेनासागरमक्षोभ्यं वेलेव समवारयत् ॥

meaning.en: But Bhimasena, in battle, held back that unshaken sea of troops like another great ocean, as the shore holds back the sea.

verses.text:
तदाश्चर्यमपश्याम श्रद्धेयमपि चाद्भुतम् ।
भीमसेनस्य समरे राजन्कर्मातिमानुषम् ॥

meaning.en: We saw there, king, a marvel hard to believe, a superhuman deed of Bhimasena in battle.

verses.text:
उदीर्णां पृथिवीं सर्वां साश्वां सरथकुञ्जराम् ।
असंभ्रमं भीमसेनो गदया समताडयत् ॥

meaning.en: Calmly, Bhimasena struck with his mace the whole rising earth, with horses, chariots and elephants.

verses.text:
स संवार्य बलौघांस्तान्गदया रथिनां वरः ।
अतिष्ठत्तुमुले भीमो गिरिर्मेरुरिवाचलः ॥

meaning.en: Holding back those floods of troops with his mace, that best of chariot-warriors stood unmoved in the tumult like Mount Meru.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्सुतुमुले घोरे काले परमदारुणे ।
भ्रातरश्चैव पुत्राश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः ॥

meaning.en: In that tumultuous, terrible, most dreadful hour, his brothers and sons, and Dhrishtadyumna son of Prishata,

verses.text:
द्रौपदेयाभिमन्युश्च शिखण्डी च महारथः ।
न प्राजहन्भीमसेनं भये जाते महाबलम् ॥

meaning.en: Draupadi's sons, Abhimanyu, and the great chariot-warrior Shikhandi did not abandon the mighty Bhimasena, though fear arose.

verses.text:
ततः शैक्यायसीं गुर्वीं प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम् ।
अवधीत्तावकान्योधान्दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ।
पोथयन्रथवृन्दानि वाजिवृन्दानि चाभिभूः ॥

meaning.en: Then, gripping a huge, heavy mace of iron, he struck your warriors like Death with his staff, crushing masses of chariots and masses of horses, the mighty one.

verses.text:
व्यचरत्समरे भीमो युगान्ते पावको यथा ।
विनिघ्नन्समरे सर्वान्युगान्ते कालवद्विभुः ॥

meaning.en: Bhima moved in the battle like the fire at the end of an age, the lord killing all in battle like Time at the end of the yuga.

verses.text:
ऊरुवेगेन संकर्षन्रथजालानि पाण्डवः ।
प्रमर्दयन्गजान्सर्वान्नड्वलानीव कुञ्जरः ॥

meaning.en: The Pandava dragged along masses of chariots with the force of his thighs and ground all the elephants down, as an elephant tramples reeds.

verses.text:
मृद्नन्रथेभ्यो रथिनो गजेभ्यो गजयोधिनः ।
सादिनश्चाश्वपृष्ठेभ्यो भूमौ चैव पदातिनः ॥

meaning.en: Crushing chariot-warriors from their chariots, elephant-fighters from their elephants, horsemen from horseback, and foot soldiers on the ground,

verses.text:
तत्र तत्र हतैश्चापि मनुष्यगजवाजिभिः ।
रणाङ्गणं तदभवन्मृत्योराघातसंनिभम् ॥

meaning.en: with men, elephants and horses killed here and there, the field of battle looked like the place where Death strikes.

verses.text:
पिनाकमिव रुद्रस्य क्रुद्धस्याभिघ्नतः पशून् ।
यमदण्डोपमामुग्रामिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनाम् ।
ददृशुर्भीमसेनस्य रौद्रां विशसनीं गदाम् ॥

meaning.en: They saw Bhimasena's dreadful, slaughtering mace, like the staff of Yama, sounding like Indra's thunderbolt, like the Pinaka of enraged Rudra striking beasts.

verses.text:
आविध्यतो गदां तस्य कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः ।
बभौ रूपं महाघोरं कालस्येव युगक्षये ॥

meaning.en: As the great-souled son of Kunti whirled his mace, he took on a most terrible form, like Time at the destruction of the age.

verses.text:
तं तथा महतीं सेनां द्रावयन्तं पुनः पुनः ।
दृष्ट्वा मृत्युमिवायान्तं सर्वे विमनसोऽभवन् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him scattering that great army again and again, like Death coming, all were dispirited.

verses.text:
यतो यतः प्रेक्षते स्म गदामुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ।
तेन तेन स्म दीर्यन्ते सर्वसैन्यानि भारत ॥

meaning.en: Wherever the Pandava turned his eyes with raised mace, Bharata, there all the armies were torn apart.

verses.text:
प्रदारयन्तं सैन्यानि बलौघेनापराजितम् ।
ग्रसमानमनीकानि व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Vrikodara of terrible deeds, unconquered, tearing the armies with his flood of strength, swallowing the divisions like Death with open mouth, with his huge mace in hand,

verses.text:
तं तथा भीमकर्माणं प्रगृहीतमहागदम् ।
दृष्ट्वा वृकोदरं भीष्मः सहसैव समभ्ययात् ॥

meaning.en: Bhishma suddenly rode at him.

verses.text:
महता मेघघोषेण रथेनादित्यवर्चसा ।
छादयञ्शरवर्षेण पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान् ॥

meaning.en: On a chariot with a great sound like thunder, bright as the sun, he covered him with a rain of arrows like Parjanya raining.

verses.text:
तमायान्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम् ।
भीष्मं भीमो महाबाहुः प्रत्युदीयादमर्षणः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Bhishma coming like Death with open mouth, mighty-armed Bhima, unforgiving, went to meet him.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्क्षणे सात्यकिः सत्यसंधः
शिनिप्रवीरोऽभ्यपतत्पितामहम् ।
निघ्नन्नमित्रान्धनुषा दृढेन
स कम्पयंस्तव पुत्रस्य सेनाम् ॥

meaning.en: At that moment Satyaki, true to his word, hero of the Shinis, rushed at the grandsire, killing enemies with his strong bow and shaking your son's army.

verses.text:
तं यान्तमश्वै रजतप्रकाशैः
शरान्धमन्तं धनुषा दृढेन ।
नाशक्नुवन्वारयितुं तदानीं
सर्वे गणा भारत ये त्वदीयाः ॥

meaning.en: As he came with his silver-bright horses, shooting arrows with his strong bow, none of your troops, Bharata, could then stop him.

verses.text:
अविध्यदेनं निशितैः शराग्रै-
रलम्बुसो राजवरार्श्यशृङ्गिः ।
तं वै चतुर्भिः प्रतिविध्य वीरो
नप्ता शिनेरभ्यपतद्रथेन ॥

meaning.en: Alambusa, the lord of the rakshasas, pierced him with sharp arrow-tips, but the hero, Shini's grandson, struck back with four and attacked him from his chariot.

verses.text:
अन्वागतं वृष्णिवरं निशम्य
मध्ये रिपूणां परिवर्तमानम् ।
प्रावर्तयन्तं कुरुपुंगवांश्च
पुनः पुनश्च प्रणदन्तमाजौ ॥

meaning.en: Bhurishravas, seeing the Vrishni hero following, wheeling in the midst of enemies, driving the Kuru bulls back, and roaring again and again in battle,

verses.text:
नाशक्नुवन्वारयितुं वरिष्ठं
मध्यंदिने सूर्यमिवातपन्तम् ।
न तत्र कश्चिन्नविषण्ण आसी-
दृते राजन्सोमदत्तस्य पुत्रात् ॥

meaning.en: they could not hold back that best of warriors, blazing like the midday sun. There was no one there who was not downcast, except Somadatta's son.

verses.text:
स ह्याददानो धनुरुग्रवेगं
भूरिश्रवा भारत सौमदत्तिः ।
दृष्ट्वा रथान्स्वान्व्यपनीयमाना-
न्प्रत्युद्ययौ सात्यकिं योद्धुमिच्छन् ॥

meaning.en: For Bhurishravas, Somadatta's son, Bharata, taking up his fast and fierce bow and seeing his own chariots being driven away, went out to meet Satyaki, wishing to fight.
